q: Why does the Guan et al. 2022 abstract report the BGYT1 genome as 2,476,083 bp while the paper's body text and both NCBI records (GCF_023276655.1, GCA_023276655.1) report 2,453,694 bp (a 22,389-bp / 0.9% discrepancy in a species-announcement paper)?
basis: Directly observed during independent replication: our own contig-summation of the deposited FASTA yields 2,453,694 bp exactly, matching the paper's own Results section but contradicting the abstract by 22 kb. This is not tool drift — it is a paper-internal contradiction that survived peer review.
next_steps: 1) Programmatically audit ~500 species-announcement papers in Arch Microbiol / IJSEM / IJSEM-online 2020-2025: extract genome length from abstract, from body text, and from linked NCBI assembly; flag mismatches >0.5%. 2) If abstract-vs-deposit mismatches are common (>5% of papers), propose a mandatory abstract-vs-deposit consistency check for taxonomic novelty announcements. 3) Contact the corresponding author (Mi Kyung Lee, KRIBB) via KRIBB corresponding-author records to request an erratum for this specific paper.

q: Why is the paper's OrthoANIu-based ANI (76.8%) systematically 3-7 percentage points lower than fastANI (80.8%), skani (79.4%), and BLASTn-based ANIb (83.4%) for the same BGYT1 vs. P. umbonata genome pair?
basis: Live-measured during replication: all three independent modern ANI tools agree with each other to within ~4 pp and all disagree with the paper's value by a similar direction and magnitude. This is not noise — it looks like a systematic tool-family difference at cross-genus divergences.
next_steps: 1) Curate a set of 30-50 published genome pairs across the 75-90% ANI band where authors reported EzBioCloud OrthoANIu and the raw FASTAs are public. 2) Recompute all pairs with fastANI, skani, ANIb, ANIm, pyani-ANIblastall, and JSpeciesWS OrthoANI. 3) Fit a regression of OrthoANIu vs. each modern method as a function of true divergence to see whether OrthoANIu has a documented systematic bias below ~85% ANI. 4) If confirmed, propose that at cross-genus divergences (where species delineation is not at stake anyway), papers should report at least two ANI methods.

q: The paper claims BGYT1 encodes chitinases and beta-1,3-glucanases (motivating a plant-fungal-pathogen biocontrol application), but the current NCBI PGAP v6.11 annotation of the same deposited assembly contains ZERO chitinase and ZERO explicit beta-1,3-glucanase gene calls. Is the paper's claim a Prokka-vs-PGAP annotation-tool artifact, a looser homology threshold, or a misannotation?
basis: Directly observed: grep -Ei 'chitinase|glucanase' on the current PGAP GFF returns 0 chitinase hits and 0 explicit beta-1,3-glucanase hits, despite finding 54 peptidases (which DOES support the paper's protease claim). The paper stated it used Prokka + KEGG-Decoder + RAST, none of which are in the current PGAP pipeline.
next_steps: 1) Re-run Prokka v1.14.6 with default databases on GCF_023276655.1 FASTA and grep for chitinase/glucanase. 2) Run dbCAN2/dbCAN3 CAZyme HMM prediction on the same proteins to get GH-family assignments independent of PGAP name-matching. 3) BLASTp the 1761 CDS against the CAZy chitinase (GH18/GH19) HMM library and the beta-1,3-glucanase (GH16/GH17/GH64/GH72/GH81) families with an explicit E-value cutoff and report all hits. 4) If Prokka + dbCAN also find zero, publish a correction indicating the biocontrol motivation is not supported. If they find hits, document the annotation-tool sensitivity of this class of biocontrol-motivating claims across the Arch Microbiol species-announcement corpus.

q: The paper states BGYT1 is 'Gram-stain-negative' in the same document where it describes the Olsenella genus (phylum Actinobacteria) as 'Gram stain positive'. Actinobacteria are canonically Gram-positive. Is BGYT1's Gram-negative reaction a genuine atypical trait (worth investigating as a taxonomic character), a Gram-stain artifact for a rod with a thin wall, or a paper transcription error?
basis: Textual contradiction observed inside the paper itself: Introduction defines Olsenella cells as 'Gram stain positive', but the Abstract and Description sections describe BGYT1 as 'Gram-stain-negative'. Cannot be checked from sequence data alone.
next_steps: 1) Order the type strain KCTC 25379T from the Korean Collection for Type Cultures (~US$150) and re-do a Gram stain independently. 2) If genuinely Gram-negative, do TEM cross-sections to look for an outer membrane (Actinobacteria with genuine outer membranes would be extraordinary). 3) If wall-integrity/thin-wall artifact, do KOH-string test as a cross-check. 4) If confirmed artifact, publish an erratum; if confirmed atypical, this is a genuinely publishable follow-up characterizing a novel wall architecture in a family where it is unexpected.

q: The paper's closest 16S relative (Olsenella umbonata KCTC 15140T, 98.24% identity) has been reclassified to Parafannyhessea umbonata (Zgheib et al. 2021, cited by the paper itself). Should Olsenella intestinalis (BGYT1) therefore be re-placed into Parafannyhessea rather than Olsenella?
basis: Observed during replication: NCBI now labels the KCTC 15140T type-strain sequences and assembly (AJ251324.3, GCF_900105025.1) as Parafannyhessea umbonata. The paper's own body text acknowledges the paraphyly of Olsenella and cites the reclassification, yet chose to name the new species in Olsenella anyway. Our own NJ tree of 13 type strains puts BGYT1 in a sub-clade with Parafannyhessea umbonata and Olsenella profusa, with the other Olsenella species (uli, absiana, porci, congonensis) forming a separate clade.
next_steps: 1) Submit a full genome set (BGYT1 + all 13+ Olsenella / Parafannyhessea / Fannyhessea / Lancefieldella / Paratractidigestivibacter type strains) to TYGS for a proper GBDP phylogenomic tree. 2) Compute a 400-marker bcgTree or GTDB-Tk-style protein-marker tree over the same set. 3) If BGYT1 clades with Parafannyhessea rather than Olsenella sensu stricto, publish a taxonomic emendation reclassifying Olsenella intestinalis as Parafannyhessea intestinalis (this is exactly the kind of update the LPSN encourages for post-reclassification announcement papers). 4) More broadly, curate the ~30 Olsenella species-announcement papers 2015-2025 and audit whether any need Parafannyhessea reclassification post-Zgheib 2021.
